definitions.explanation: Physical currency as opposed to credit.

examples.japanese: {現金|げんきん}を{持|も}っていない。
examples.english: I don't have cash on me.

examples.japanese: ATMで{現金|げんきん}を{下|お}ろした。
examples.english: I withdrew cash from the ATM.

examples.japanese: このお{店|みせ}はカードが{使|つか}えないので、{現金|げんきん}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: This shop doesn't accept cards, so you need cash.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}は{現金|げんきん}を{使|つか}う{人|ひと}が{減|へ}って、{電子|でんし}マネーで{払|はら}う{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えた。
examples.english: Recently, fewer people use cash and more people pay with electronic money.

notes:
{現金|げんきん} refers to physical currency (bills and coins) as opposed to digital or credit-based payments.

COMPONENTS:
- {現|げん}: present, current, actual
- {金|きん}: money, gold

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {現金|げんきん}で{払|はら}う (to pay in cash)
- {現金|げんきん}を{引|ひ}き{出|だ}す (to withdraw cash)
- {現金|げんきん}を{下|おろ}す (to withdraw cash - colloquial)
- {現金|げんきん}{払|ばら}い (cash payment)
- {現金|げんきん}のみ (cash only)

CONTRAST WITH OTHER PAYMENT METHODS:
- {現金|げんきん}: cash (physical money)
- クレジットカード: credit card
- {電子|でんし}マネー: electronic money (Suica, PayPay, etc.)
- {振|ふ}り{込|こ}み: bank transfer
- {小切手|こぎって}: check

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan has traditionally been a cash-heavy society, though digital payments have grown rapidly. Many small shops and restaurants still prefer {現金|げんきん}.
